posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
we need some numbers before we can even guess what's happening.
what is the screen size of the game screen, and what is the screen size of the video?
which player(s) have you tried to use (default or plugin?)
The engine cannot display a video that has a greater screen size than the game screen, if that is tried the result is either nothing or a resized video depending on the player code.
As a side note, those numbers are always screen sizes, never resolutions. technically a resolution is something with dpi (dots per inch) or ppi (pixels per inch): a single number, never an area of two numbers. And that difference may become important when discussing display- or video formats.
So it's better to clear that up in advance.

because no form of video editing can change the aspect ratio without distorting the image.
Example:
Take a single screenshot of the video, use any image program to increase its horizontal size to the one needed for your screen width without distortions, then try to see it: instead of black borders to the left and right, part of the picture on top and bottom will be cut off because that part (sky and grass) no longer fit the screen completely.
you could check the same with windows photo display (or however that program is called in your language: try to find a zoom that fits your screen and you'll see that that is impossible, either the zoom is to low (and and the picture doesn't reach from left to right) or the zoom is too high (and top and bottom are cut off).

you CANNOT stretch a video into a different aspect ratio.
How often do we have to write that for you to understand?
To change the aspect ratio you either have to create new data (by giving the video/picture to an artist to add new parts to the left and right) or cut away part of it from top and bottom.

posts.author: ElvenNeko
posts.body:
bass2yang said:
Having the video with the proper width/height is preferable over stretching the video or making changes with it using html/js/css/etc.
(Not sure if the others covered this already - haven't fully checked out the links/posts)
In any case, assuming you are using the normal "Play Video" event command or using the basic video player in MV/MZ, one possibility I can think of is running this code in a script call when playing your video (run the script call before playing the video or during the video being played so you can see it - use DevTools to see the difference if it is working):
JavaScript:
const s     = Graphics._video.style;
s.objectFit = 'cover';
s.minWidth  = '100%';
s.minHeight = '100%';
Hope this helps.
Click to expand...
